What is Log Poisoning?

Log Poisoning is a technique where an attacker injects malicious PHP code into a server log file and then uses a Local File Inclusion (LFI) vulnerability to include that log file, causing the injected code to execute.
This works because PHP parses any file included via <highlight>include()</highlight> or <highlight>require()</highlight> as PHP source code, regardless of its file extension.

Step 4 - Trigger Code Execution
Multiple Payload Execution
If the payload appears multiple times inside the log file, it executes multiple times because PHP parses the entire file and runs every <?php ?> block it encounters.
Why This Works

title: Execution Mechanism
items: include() reads the entire file, not line by line.
PHP parses the file regardless of its extension.
Text outside PHP tags is printed.
Repeated payloads result in repeated execution.

text: Conclusion

Log Poisoning transforms an LFI vulnerability into Remote Code Execution by injecting PHP into writable logs and forcing the application to include them. The attack succeeds because the application blindly includes attacker-controlled content without validation.
